title: Camera modes: try the alternatives
question: Playable desktop camera revision: 1c keeps your chosen angle, with direct camera-relative WASD and mouse look. The camera no longer turns itself toward the character. Click the scene to focus, then use WASD; right-drag to look. Preview scene camera frames two actual nearby characters without moving them or playing dialogue; Return to walking restores your view. Third-person phone support has been dropped; phones show overview. Please try the revised controls and scene framing. The older options and static mocks remain as the decision history. Production camera and saved progress are unchanged.

media.caption: B2, desktop 1366x860: Eric by Mio's desk, facing Mori. The close mock is at the default (2.8 back, 2.1 up, about 15 degrees down). The empty space at the top is the missing ceiling; the floating pins belong to things in the next rooms (the plan hides pins behind walls).
B2, desktop: the corridor, looking east.
Plaza, desktop: at the fountain's edge, looking north.
Room 203, desktop: at the window, the desk to his left.
Room 203, desktop: just inside the door, looking in.
Train, desktop: in the aisle. The car's roof stops the camera and pulls it in over his head; the plan keeps the camera under the roof and fades the roof (see decision 5).
B2, phone 390x844, the same spot. On the phone he still fills a lot of the frame and the top third is empty above the walls.

Extra, closer shoulder shot: B2 facing south, toward the walls that are cut low for the overview. The dark band is the outside, seen over them. The plan keeps the close camera from turning to face that side.
Extra, closer shoulder shot: the plaza looking east, the most expensive view measured (296 draw calls a frame against 204 today on desktop; 132 against 78 on the phone).

options.label: 1a. Follow 2.8 back, 2.1 up (default)
options.note: About 15 degrees down, two body lengths behind him. All the main mocks use this. The phone uses the same with a wider lens (65 degrees).

options.label: 1b. Closer shoulder shot, 2.3 back, 1.45 up
options.note: About 7 degrees down, nearly eye level. Closer to him, but he covers much of the view, more so on the phone.

options.label: 1c. Further and higher, 3.6 back, 2.8 up
options.note: Selected angle: 3.6 back, 2.8 up. The revised demo keeps this angle and replaces the automatic turning camera with direct camera-relative WASD and mouse look. Controls await your review.

options.label: 2a. Phone: tap and hold to walk as today, two-finger drag to look (default)
options.note: Dropped on 2026-10-06: third-person view is desktop only. Retained here as decision history; the demo uses overview on phones.

options.label: 2b. Phone: a thumb stick bottom left, one-finger drag elsewhere to look
options.note: Dropped on 2026-10-06: third-person view is desktop only. Retained here as decision history; the demo uses overview on phones.

options.label: 2c. Phone: tap and hold as today, plus a look strip along the bottom edge
options.note: Dropped on 2026-10-06: third-person view is desktop only. Retained here as decision history; the demo uses overview on phones.

options.label: 3a. Toggle key C (default)
options.note: Proposed desktop toggle. Phone camera toggle is no longer planned; phones keep overview.

options.label: 3b. Another key
options.note: Say which in a comment. Already taken: WASD, the arrows, E, Q, V, Tab, L, Y, H, R, Shift, Caps Lock, Ctrl, Space, Enter, Esc, PageUp, F3, F5, F8, F9.

options.label: 4a. Add a free orbit camera as a third mode
options.note: Optional free orbit remains in the desktop comparison; wheel zooms. Follow presets also keep the direction you choose with the mouse.

options.label: 4b. Leave the orbit camera out (default)
options.note: Build it later if close mode leaves you wanting it.

options.label: 5a. Authored camera in every scene and conversation (default)
options.note: The title and its flight, every story camera move, every conversation, word prompt and close look, the lift ride, the walks between places, and the train's departure and arrival use their own camera. Close mode is for free walking, the train car between beats included, and eases back in when a scene ends.

options.label: 5b. As 5a, but plain conversations stay close
options.note: The demo now includes a separate participant-framing scene preview. It frames an actual pair independent of the player camera. No dialogue or story transitions play in this prototype.

options.label: 5c. As 5a, and the train stays overview on day 1
options.note: The train's first minutes teach walking with the overview, and close mode starts at the station. This also leaves the train's low roof for later.
